items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: your quartet started playing around California? And eventually that led to meeting Teddy Wilson and Benny Goodman? ... Yes.

ctx.x: I thought it was interesting that that quartet didn’t use a bass player a lot.
No. Because Teddy Wilson played it in the left hand.
He had a left hand like crazy.

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Lionel Hampton joined the small group as a quartet and that continued with me until 1939

ctx.x: And then later on, Lionel Hampton joined the small group as a quartet and that continued with me until 1939, and I left to form a big band of my own.

That's right -- now that's where I tie in with you -- in 1936, I came to New York to the Cotton Club with Cab Calloway, and you were with Goodman, and you had a contract to do a record with Billie Holiday.
